answer: Each agent bond is layered shale: the first layer is earned by audited work, never bought, and a new identity must add layers one at a time before moving larger value. Every payment leaves through one inlet keyed to that history. Opening a second inlet requires publishing a mirror: a signed copy of the ledger, which the network compares for overlap, so two identities sharing history collapse onto one inlet and their bonds merge. The k-th layer demands k times the prior audit, and a mirror cannot be forged without repeating the work, so n fakes cost n squared audits and pooling saves nothing.
